---
title: "Updating and backups"
description: "Update a local OmicsBase install, stay on one version, back it up, move it or remove it."
---

## Update {#update}

Run the install command again:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/main/install.sh | sh
```

If you installed into another folder, give the same `OMICSBASE_DIR` again. See [Install-time settings](settings.qmd#install-time).

The update:

- **keeps** your accounts, notes and files (`data/`) and your settings (`.env`), including the version you pinned;
- **adds** to `.env` any secret that the new version needs;
- **replaces** the setup files `docker-compose.yml`, `librechat.yaml`, `reports-gate.Caddyfile`, `import_examples.js` and `.env.example` with fresh copies, so changes you made to them are lost;
- **downloads** the new images and restarts OmicsBase with them.

The example notes are downloaded only if they are missing.

## Pin a version {#pin}

By default, an install follows `latest`, the newest version. To stay on one version, run the install command with that version in front of `sh`, for example:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/main/install.sh | OMICSBASE_VERSION=2026.11.20 sh
```

The installer writes the version into `~/omicsbase/.env`, takes the setup files released with that version, and downloads its images. When you update later, give the same `OMICSBASE_VERSION` again, so the setup files match your version too.

If the installer prints `Note: no files are released under …`, it found no setup files for that version and uses the newest ones with your version's images. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#no-release-files).

To follow the newest version again:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/main/install.sh | OMICSBASE_VERSION=latest sh
```

If you run notes on your own server, set the same version in the server's `.env`. See [Notes engine on a server](engine-server.qmd#update).

## Back up {#backup}

Everything that is yours is in two places in the install folder:

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `data/` | Accounts, notes, files, Reports work, the app's own keys and caches |
| `.env` | Your settings and secrets |

The setup files and `examples/` are downloaded again by the installer, so they need no backup.

Stop OmicsBase before you copy, so the database is not written to during the copy:

```bash
cd ~/omicsbase
docker compose down
tar czf ~/omicsbase-backup.tgz data .env
docker compose up -d
```

The backup contains your secrets and everyone's notes. Keep it as private as the install itself.

Some files in `data/projects/` and `data/reports/` are written by Reports, which runs as another user in your group. If `tar` reports `Permission denied` for some of them on Linux, run the `tar` command with `sudo`.

`data/engine-cache/` holds downloaded ExperimentHub and AnnotationHub data. It can be large, and it is downloaded again when needed, so you can leave it out of the backup:

```bash
tar czf ~/omicsbase-backup.tgz --exclude=data/engine-cache data .env
```

### Restore {#restore}

1. Stop OmicsBase: `cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose down`.
2. Move the current `data/` and `.env` aside.
3. Unpack the backup in the install folder:

   ```bash
   cd ~/omicsbase && tar xzf ~/omicsbase-backup.tgz
   ```

4. Start OmicsBase: `docker compose up -d`.

## Move to another machine {#move}

The installer keeps any `data/` and `.env` it finds in the install folder, so you can move an install by copying them.

1. On the old machine, make a [backup](#backup).
2. Copy `omicsbase-backup.tgz` to the new machine.
3. On the new machine, unpack it into the install folder:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/omicsbase && cd ~/omicsbase && tar xzf ~/omicsbase-backup.tgz
   ```

4. Check your user and group id on the new machine with `id -u` and `id -g`. If they differ from `UID` and `GID` in `~/omicsbase/.env`, change them there.
5. Run the install command. It keeps the copied `data/` and `.env`, downloads the rest and starts OmicsBase.

If you run notes on your own server, the server keeps working with the moved install, because `.env` keeps the same `ENGINE_URL` and secret.

## Uninstall {#uninstall}

Each step removes more. Stop after the step you need.

**1. Stop and remove the containers.** Keeps your data, settings and the downloaded images.

```bash
cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose down
```

**2. Also remove the images.** Frees most of the disk space (about 25 GB). Keeps your data and settings; the next install downloads the images again.

```bash
cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose down --rmi all
```

**3. Also delete your data.** This permanently deletes every account, note, uploaded file and report on this install, and your settings and secrets. It cannot be undone. Make a [backup](#backup) first if you may want any of it.

```bash
rm -rf ~/omicsbase
```

Some files in `data/projects/` and `data/reports/` are written by Reports, which runs as another user in your group. If `rm` reports `Permission denied` for some of them on Linux, run the same command with `sudo`.

If you ran notes on your own server, remove it there too, in its `omicsbase-engine` folder: `docker compose down --rmi all`, then delete the folder. Its `data/` holds the files of notes that ran there.
